title: The Drake Equation and SETI
welcome_lead: Estimating how many civilisations might be out there.
meta_desc: A-Level Astronomy: Drake equation factors, Fermi paradox, SETI.

concepts.def: N = R* x fp x ne x fl x fi x fc x L.
Estimated number of communicating civilisations in the Milky Way.
R* — the average rate of star formation in the galaxy.
If life is likely, where is everyone?
L — duration over which a civilisation emits detectable signals.

walkthroughs.body_html: Frank Drake (1961) proposed N = R* x fp x ne x fl x fi x fc x L. The first three factors are now well constrained; the rest are highly uncertain — especially the lifetime L of communicating civilisations.
If even modest values give many civilisations, where is everyone? Possible answers range from cosmic 'great filters' to short civilisation lifetimes to deliberate silence.
SETI programmes scan radio bands for narrow, artificial signals. Big-data efforts like Breakthrough Listen now examine millions of stars; no confirmed signal has been detected so far.
